new_entities.name: CoQ10 supplementation during IVF
new_entities.description: Coenzyme Q10 supplementation before or during IVF or ICSI treatment.

new_entities.name: Oocyte quality
new_entities.description: Quality or competence of retrieved oocytes, often inferred through aneuploidy, fertilization, embryo quality, or related embryological outcomes.

edges.effect_quant: The best human trial evidence is suggestive but underpowered. In low-prognosis young women with decreased ovarian reserve, CoQ10 pretreatment improved fertilization and high-quality embryo counts in a 186-patient RCT, while the smaller placebo-controlled aneuploidy trial showed a numerically lower oocyte aneuploidy rate without statistical certainty. A newer 100-patient randomized study found better oocyte counts and ovarian response but no significant clinical-pregnancy difference.
edges.population: women undergoing IVF or ICSI, especially those with poor ovarian reserve or poor ovarian response
edges.mechanism: CoQ10 is involved in mitochondrial electron transport and antioxidant defense, making it biologically plausible as a support for oocyte energy metabolism and chromosomal competence. The central uncertainty is whether those mitochondrial gains are large enough to produce reliable human clinical benefits beyond small embryology improvements.
edges.summary: This is a plausible but not yet definitive IVF optimization edge. CoQ10 may improve some oocyte or embryo-quality markers, particularly in poor-reserve populations, but the clinical evidence is still too thin and underpowered for a stronger claim.
edges.caveats: Several studies are small, enriched for selected poor-reserve populations, or terminated early. This edge should stay focused on oocyte-quality signals rather than be inflated into a proven live-birth enhancer.

evidence.citation: XuY et al 2018 Reprod Biol Endocrinol
evidence.notes: Pretreatment with coenzyme Q10 improves ovarian response and embryo quality in low-prognosis young women with decreased ovarian reserve: a randomized controlled trial.
